# edge 93 — intro + refined sound design
Clock.bpm = 93
Root.default = "A#"

# === INTRO: fog — harmonic DNA emerges from nothing ===
p1 >> darkpad([0, 6], dur=8, oct=4, sus=8, atk=4, dark=0.7, detune=0.02, amp=linvar([0, 0.35], 32), lpf=linvar([300, 1200], 64), room=0.9, mix=0.7)
p2 >> ethpad([0, 1, 7], dur=8, oct=5, attack=4, release=4, amp=linvar([0, 0.3], 48), room=0.9, mix=0.6)

# === INTRO 2: c2 arpeggio barely audible, drowned in reverb ===
c2 >> cs80([0, 0, 0.5], cutoff=linvar([200, 1500], [16, 8, 16]), dec=1.0, leg=0, oct=(3, PStep(4, 3, 4)), vibspeed=P[0.5, 2, 0.5, 1.1], vibdepth=0.1, lpf=linvar([200, 1200], 64), dur=1/6, shape=0, amp=var([0, 0.15], [24, 8]), room=0.7, mix=0.5).unison(2)

# === INTRO 3: c1 enters filtered, delay pulls it wide ===
c1 >> cs80(cutoff=linvar([400, 3000], [8, 4, 8]), dec=1.0, leg=var([0, 4], [31, 1]), lpr=0.1, oct=(4, PStep(4, 3, 4)), vibspeed=P[0.5, 2, 0.5, 1.1], vibdepth=0.1, lpf=linvar([400, 2000], 64), dur=1/6, shape=0, room=0.5, mix=0.3, amp=linvar([0, 0.5], 32), delay=PSine(128)*0.33)

# === MAIN: edge arrives — lo-fi bite but with space ===
c1.bits = 8
c1.crush = var([8, 5], [12, 4])
c1.shape = 0.2
c1.fx1 = 1
c1.glide = 1
c1.lpf = linvar([400, 4000], 128)

# c2 — tape warmth instead of raw dist2, shimmer for depth
c2 >> cs80([0, 0, 0.5], cutoff=linvar([400, 5300], [8, 4, 8]), dec=1.0, leg=0, lpr=0.1, oct=(3, PStep(4, 3, 4)), vibspeed=P[0.5, 2, 0.5, 1.1], vibdepth=0.1, lpf=linvar([400, 4000], 128), glide=3, dur=1/6, shape=0.1, tape=var([0, 0.8], [8, 8]), tapedrive=var([1, 3], [12, 4]), shimmer=var([0, 0.5], [16, 16]), shimsize=0.6, shimpitch=var([1, 2], [8, 8]), shimmix=0.3, room=0.4, mix=0.25).unison(3)

# pad opens — shimmer bloom
p1.shimmer = 0.5
p1.shimsize = 0.6
p1.shimpitch = var([1, 2, 1.5], [8, 4, 4])
p1.shimmix = 0.4
p1.amp = 0.3

# f-family #120
# documentation
  
  # === F-FAMILY — Raccourcis pour patterns et timevars ===                                                                               
  # Signature unifiée: f?(n=16, a=0, b=1)                                                                                               
  # n = durée en beats (timevars) ou longueur (patterns)                                                                                  
  # a = valeur min, b = valeur max                                                                                                        
  # Sans args: valeurs par défaut (16, 0, 1)                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                          
  # fi — fade in: monte de a vers b, puis reste (linvar)                                                                                  
p1 >> sinepad([0,4,7], dur=4, amp=fi())  # amp monte de 0 à 1 sur 16 beats                                                              
p1 >> sinepad([0,4,7], dur=4, lpf=fi(32, 200, 8000))  # filtre s'ouvre de 200 à 8000 sur 32 beats                                       
                                                                                                                                          
  # fo — fade out: descend de b vers a, puis reste (linvar inversé)
p1.amp = fo(8)  # fade out sur 8 beats, de 1 à 0
p1.lpf = fo(48, 400, 4000)  # filtre se ferme de 4000 à 400 sur 48 beats

# fb — fade bounce: oscille entre a et b en boucle (linvar cyclique)
b1 >> dbass([0,3,5], dur=1/2, lpf=fb(16, 400, 3000))  # filtre wah-wah entre 400 et 3000
b1.dist2 = fb(8, 0, 0.6)  # distortion qui respire entre 0 et 0.6

# fe — fade exponentiel: monte de a vers b avec courbe exponentielle (expvar)
p1.amp = fe(32)  # fade in lent au début, rapide à la fin
b1.lpf = fe(16, 200, 6000)  # ouverture de filtre exponentielle

  # fs — fade sinusoïdal: oscille doucement entre a et b (sinvar)
j1 >> blip(pan = fs(8, -1, 1))  # auto-pan sinusoïdal gauche/droite sur 8 beats
p1.amp = fs(32, 0.3, 0.7)  # volume qui pulse doucement

# fr — random: valeurs aléatoires entre a et b (PWhite) - répétés comme un [:8]
d1 >> play("-", dur=1/4, amp=fr(8, 0.2, 0.8))  # 8 amplitudes aléatoires entre 0.2 et 0.8
j1.pan = fr(16, -1, 1)  # panoramique aléatoire, cycle de 16

# fw — walk: marche aléatoire bornée (PWalk)
j1 >> plaitsX(fw(12, 1, 7), dur=1/4)  # mélodie en marche aléatoire, step de 1, max 7, répétion 12 foix
  b1.degree = fw(8, 1, 4)  # basse qui se promène doucement

 # fg — gaussien: distribution gaussienne (PGauss)
j1.fmod = fg(8, 0, 0.2)  # modulation FM gaussienne, centrée sur 0, écart 0.2, répétition 8 x

# ft — triangulaire: distribution triangulaire (PTrir)
j1 >> cs80(ft(8, 0, 12), dur=PDur(3,8))  # mélodie en distribution triangulaire 0-12

# fc — coin flip: pile ou face entre a et b (PCoin)
d1.amp = fc(8, 0, 1)  # chaque step est soit 0 soit 1 (gate aléatoire)
j1.oct = 4 + fc(8, 0, 1)  # alterne aléatoirement entre octave 4 et 5

# fq — onde sinusoïdale: un cycle de sinus mappé sur a-b (PSine)
p1.lpf = fq(32, 200, 8000)  # filtre qui suit une courbe sinusoïdale complète
d2.amp = fq(16, 0.2, 0.8)  # amplitude en forme de vague

# fz — dent de scie: un cycle de sawtooth mappé sur a-b (PSaw)
b1.lpf = fz(16, 400, 4000)  # filtre en dent de scie (montée linéaire, chute)

  # === Combinaisons ===
  # Multiplication: fi() * 4 → rampe de 0 à 4
b1 >> lbass([0,5], dur=1, amp=fi()*0.8, lpf=fb(16, 200, 2000)*fr(8, 1, 3))

  # Tableaux dans n: durées asymétriques (timevars seulement)
c1.lpf = fb([8,4], 400, 3000)  # monte sur 8 beats, redescend sur 4
c1.cutoff = fi([16,8,16], 200, 5000)  # rythme irrégulier de sweep

# Addition: fi() + 3 → rampe de 3 à 4
j1.oct = fw(16, 1, 3) + 4  # marche aléatoire autour d'octave 4-7

# svdk - Raw Rolling Bass Synth

Inspired by Daft Punk "Rollin' & Scratchin'" - Juno-106 + Boss MT-2 Metal Zone character.
With stereo drift, harmonic control, and solid low-end body.

## Sound Design

- **Oscillators**: 3 detuned saws (Juno-style) + white/pink noise
- **Harmonics**: Controllable upper partials (2nd, 3rd, 5th)
- **Sub layer**: Deep sine (2 oct down) + sine sub + pulse sub + triangle (parallel bass path)
- **Filter**: Resonant lowpass with envelope and keyboard tracking
- **Distortion**: 4-stage Boss MT-2 style (soft sat → hard clip → fold → tanh)
- **EQ**: Double bass shelf boost, slight mid cut, upper presence
- **Stereo**: Drift with independent L/R LFOs, pitch drift, subtle delay widening

## Parameters

| Parameter | Range | Default | Description |
|-----------|-------|---------|-------------|
| grit | 0-1 | 0.5 | Distortion amount (clean → MT-2 cranked) |
| noise | 0-1 | 0.3 | White/pink noise mix |
| cutoff | 100-8000 | 800 | Filter cutoff frequency |
| res | 0-1 | 0.5 | Filter resonance |
| track | 0-2 | 1 | Keyboard tracking on filter |
| fenv | 0-1 | 0.3 | Filter envelope depth |
| slide | 0-0.5 | 0.05 | Portamento/glide time |
| body | 0-1 | 0.5 | Low-end weight/thickness |
| drift | 0-1 | 0.3 | Stereo movement (0=static, 1=wide) |
| harm | 0-1 | 0.2 | Upper harmonics (2nd, 3rd, 5th) |

---

## Usage Examples by Genre

### Daft Punk - Homework Era

```python
# === DA FUNK style ===
# Single root note pumping with kick, filter opens slowly
# Original: G minor, 303 through distortion

s1 >> svdk([0], dur=0.5, sus=0.4, oct=3, grit=0.7, res=0.4,
           cutoff=linvar([400, 1200], 16), body=0.8, noise=0.1)

# === ROLLIN' & SCRATCHIN' ===
# Sustained note, filter sweep IS the melody
# Max noise, high resonance, heavy distortion

s1 >> svdk([0], dur=8, sus=8, oct=3, grit=0.9, noise=0.8, res=0.7,
           cutoff=linvar([150, 4000], 8), body=0.7, drift=0.5, fenv=0)

# === REVOLUTION 909 ===
# Pumping bassline, tight and punchy

s1 >> svdk([0,0,0,[-2,0]], dur=0.5, sus=0.3, oct=3, grit=0.5,
           cutoff=600, res=0.3, body=0.9, slide=0.02)

# === AROUND THE WORLD ===
# Disco-funk bassline, slides between notes, ghost notes
# E minor, Dorian scale feel

# svdk - Raw Rolling Bass Synth

Inspired by Daft Punk "Rollin' & Scratchin'" - Juno-106 + Boss MT-2 Metal Zone character.
With stereo drift, harmonic control, and solid low-end body.

## Sound Design

- **Oscillators**: 3 detuned saws (Juno-style) + white/pink noise
- **Harmonics**: Controllable upper partials (2nd, 3rd, 5th)
- **Sub layer**: Deep sine (2 oct down) + sine sub + pulse sub + triangle (parallel bass path)
- **Filter**: Resonant lowpass with envelope and keyboard tracking
- **Distortion**: 4-stage Boss MT-2 style (soft sat → hard clip → fold → tanh)
- **EQ**: Double bass shelf boost, slight mid cut, upper presence
- **Stereo**: Drift with independent L/R LFOs, pitch drift, subtle delay widening

## Parameters

| Parameter | Range | Default | Description |
|-----------|-------|---------|-------------|
| grit | 0-1 | 0.5 | Distortion amount (clean → MT-2 cranked) |
| noise | 0-1 | 0.3 | White/pink noise mix |
| cutoff | 100-8000 | 800 | Filter cutoff frequency |
| res | 0-1 | 0.5 | Filter resonance |
| track | 0-2 | 1 | Keyboard tracking on filter |
| fenv | 0-1 | 0.3 | Filter envelope depth |
| slide | 0-0.5 | 0.05 | Portamento/glide time |
| body | 0-1 | 0.5 | Low-end weight/thickness |
| drift | 0-1 | 0.3 | Stereo movement (0=static, 1=wide) |
| harm | 0-1 | 0.2 | Upper harmonics (2nd, 3rd, 5th) |

## 1. Generative Patterns

Algorithmic pattern generators that produce evolving, non-repeating sequences.

### PMarkov2 — Higher-order Markov chain

Analyzes an input sequence and builds N-gram transition tables. Falls back to shorter context windows when no exact match is found.

```python
# Train on a melody, generate new notes in the same style
d1 >> pluck(degree=[0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 5, 4, 2], dur=0.5)

# Order 1 = more random, order 3 = closer to source
d1 >> pluck(degree=PMarkov2([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1], order=9), dur=1/4)

# Use with scale degrees for generative melodies
d1 >> keys(degree=PMarkov2([0, 2, 4, 7, 9, 7, 4, 2, 0], order=3), sus=2, dur=1)
```

**Parameters:** `data` (source sequence), `order` (N-gram depth, default 2)

### PLife — Cellular automaton

1D elementary cellular automaton (Wolfram Rules 30, 90, 110, etc.) mapped to 0/1 values. Useful for binary rhythms and gates.

```python
# Rule 30 rhythm (chaotic)
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=30, size=16))

# Rule 110 (complex) as degree selection
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLife(rule=110, size=8) * 7, dur=0.5)

# Combine rules for layered rhythms
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=30, size=32))
d2 >> play("o", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=90, size=32))
```

**Parameters:** `rule` (rule number, default 30), `size` (grid width, default 16), `row` (starting row, default 0)

### PLSystem — L-system rewriting

L-system string rewriting mapped to numeric values. Default is Fibonacci L-system.

```python
# Default Fibonacci L-system
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLSystem(), dur=0.5)

# Custom L-system with custom mapping
d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PLSystem(
        axiom="A",
        rules={"A": "AB", "B": "A"},
        generations=8,
        mapping={"A": 0, "B": 4}
    ),
    dur=0.25
)

# Plant-like branching pattern
d1 >> keys(
    degree=PLSystem(axiom="F", rules={"F": "F+F-F"}, generations=4,
                    mapping={"F": 0, "+": 3, "-": -2}),
    dur=0.5, sus=2
)
```

**Parameters:** `axiom` (start string), `rules` (rewrite dict), `generations` (default 6), `mapping` (char-to-value dict)

### PEvolve — Genetic algorithm

Maintains a population of sequences, selects via tournament, crosses over, mutates, and walks through individuals.

```python
# Evolve a melody toward consonance
  
def consonance(seq):
    return sum(1 for x in seq if x in [0, 2, 4, 5, 7])

d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PEvolve([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], fitness=consonance, mutation=0.3),
    dur=0.5
)

# Evolve rhythmic density
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25,
    amplify=PEvolve([1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1],
                     fitness=lambda s: -abs(sum(s) - 5),  # target 5 hits
                     mutation=0.15))
```

**Parameters:** `population` (source values), `fitness` (fitness function), `mutation` (rate, default 0.1), `crossover` (rate, default 0.7), `pop_size` (default 8)

## 2. Stochastic Patterns

Probability-based and noise generators for humanization and controlled randomness.

### PGauss — Gaussian distribution

```python
# Humanized timing (slight random delay)
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.5, delay=PGauss(mean=0, sigma=0.02))

# Pitch variation around a center note
d1 >> pluck(degree=PGauss(4, 1), dur=0.5)

# Random velocity with normal distribution
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PGauss(mean=0.7, sigma=0.15))
```

**Parameters:** `mean` (center, default 0), `sigma` (std deviation, default 1)

### PBrown — Brownian motion

Constrained random walk. Each step adds a gaussian offset clamped to [lo, hi].

```python
# Drifting filter cutoff
d1 >> pluck(dur=0.5, lpf=PBrown(lo=200, hi=4000, step=100))

# Wandering pitch
d1 >> sine(degree=PBrown(lo=0, hi=7, step=1), dur=0.25)

# Slow panning drift
d1 >> pads(dur=2, pan=PBrown(lo=-1, hi=1, step=0.2))
```

**Parameters:** `lo` (lower bound, default 0), `hi` (upper bound, default 1), `step` (step size, default 0.1)

### PLogistic — Chaotic map

Logistic map: `x = r*x*(1-x)`. Produces chaos near r=3.9-4.0.

```python
# Chaotic pitch sequence
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLogistic(r=3.60, scale=1), dur=0.25)

# Edge of chaos (r=3.57 = period doubling)
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLogistic(r=3.57, scale=12, offset=-6), dur=0.5)

# Chaotic rhythm density
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLogistic(r=3.5, scale=1))
```

**Parameters:** `r` (growth rate, default 3.9), `x0` (initial value, default 0.5), `scale` (output scale, default 1), `offset` (default 0)

### PSkip — Probability gate

Passes source values with a given probability, otherwise returns a default value.

```python
# Sparse hi-hat pattern (50% chance of playing)
d1 >> play("-", dur=0.25, amplify=PSkip(P[1], prob=0.5, default=0))

# Random note omission
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 5, 7], dur=0.5,
            amplify=PSkip(P[1], prob=0.7, default=0))

# Ghost notes on snare
d2 >> play("o", dur=0.5, amplify=PSkip(P[0.3], prob=0.4, default=0))
```

**Parameters:** `pattern` (source), `prob` (probability, default 0.5), `default` (fallback value, default 0)

### PSwitch — Weighted pattern switching

Each step randomly selects one of the source patterns based on weights.

```python
# Switch between two melodies
d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PSwitch([P[0, 2, 4], P[5, 7, 9]], weights=[0.7, 0.3]),
    dur=0.5
)

# Weighted rhythm switching
d1 >> play(
    PSwitch([P["x o x o"], P["x x . x"], P["x . x ."]], weights=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2]),
    dur=0.25
)
```

**Parameters:** `patterns` (list of patterns), `weights` (selection weights, default equal)

## 3. Groove Templates

Pre-built swing, groove, and accent patterns from classic hardware.

### PSwing — Swing delay

```python
# Basic swing feel
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.25, delay=PSwing(0.1))

# Heavy swing
d1 >> play("x-o-", dur=0.25, delay=PSwing(0.4))
```

**Parameters:** `amount` (swing amount, default 0.1), `steps` (default 8)

### PGroove — Named groove templates

Available grooves: `mpc60`, `tr808`, `sp1200`, `linn`, `shuffle`, `clave`

```python
# MPC-60 feel
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("mpc60"))

# TR-808 groove
d1 >> play("x-o-x-o-", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("tr808", steps=16))

# SP-1200 timing
d1 >> play("xo", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("sp1200"))

# Clave groove
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("clave", steps=16))
```

**Parameters:** `name` (template name), `steps` (default 16)

### PAccent — Velocity accent patterns

Available accents: `backbeat`, `four_floor`, `offbeat`, `ghost`

```python
# Backbeat accents (snare on 2 and 4)
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PAccent("backbeat", steps=16))

d2 >> dbass(amp=PAccent("backbeat", steps=16), dur=1/4)  
  
# Four-on-the-floor kick emphasis
d1 >> play("V", dur=0.25, amplify=PAccent("four_floor", steps=32))

# Ghost note pattern
d2 >> play("o", dur=0.25, amplify=PAccent("ghost", steps=16))

# Combine groove + accent
d1 >> play("xo", dur=0.25,
           delay=PGroove("mpc60"),
           amplify=PAccent("backbeat"))
```

**Parameters:** `name` (template name), `steps` (default 16)

## 4. Advanced Euclidean Rhythms

Extensions to the built-in PEuclid for more complex rhythmic structures.

### PEuclidR — Rotated Euclidean

```python
# Standard Euclidean: 5 hits in 8 steps
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclid(5, 8))

d2 >> play("o", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidR(5, 8, rotation=2))


**Parameters:** `n` (pulses), `k` (steps), `rotation` (default 1)

### PEuclidFill — Layered Euclidean

OR-combines multiple Euclidean rhythms. Returns 1 where any layer has a pulse.

```python
# Layer 3-in-8 and 5-in-8
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidFill((3, 8), ([9, 3], 12)))

# Dense polyrhythmic fill
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amp=1,amplify=PEuclidFill((3, 16), (5, 8), (7, 16)))
```

**Parameters:** `*pairs` (tuples of (n, k) — all must share the same k)

### PEuclidAccent — Euclidean with accents

Two-layer Euclidean: base hits + accent layer. Returns 0 (rest), 0.5 (normal), or 1.0 (accent).

```python
# 5-in-8 with accented subset
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidAccent(5, 8, accent_n=2))

# 7-in-16 with 3 accents
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidAccent(7, 16, accent_n=3))
```

**Parameters:** `n`, `k`, `accent_n` (default n//2), `accent_k` (default k)

## 5. Polymetric Tools

Duration pattern helpers for tuplets and metric divisions.

### PMetric — N pulses in M beats

```python
# 5 evenly-spaced notes in 4 beats
d1 >> pluck(dur=PMetric(5, 4))

# 7 notes in 2 beats
d2 >> bass(dur=PMetric(7, 2))

# 3 in 1 beat (= triplet)
d3 >> keys(dur=PMetric(3, 1))
```

**Parameters:** `pulses`, `period` (default 1)

### PTriplet — Triplet shorthand

```python
# Triplets against quarter notes
d1 >> pluck(dur=1)
d2 >> pluck(dur=PTriplet(1), oct=5)

# Half-note triplets
d3 >> bass(dur=PTriplet(2))
```

**Parameters:** `dur` (default 1)

### PQuintuplet — Quintuplet shorthand

```python
# 5 notes in 2 beats
d1 >> pluck(dur=PQuintuplet(2))

# 5 in 1 beat
d2 >> pluck(dur=PQuintuplet(1), oct=5)
```

**Parameters:** `dur` (default 1)

### PPolymetric — Merged polymetric timeline

Merges multiple (pulses, value) pairs into a single interleaved timeline. Returns a dict with `dur` and `degree` patterns.

```python
# 3-against-4 polyrhythm
poly = PPolymetric((3, 0), (4, 2), total=4)
d1 >> pluck(dur=poly['dur'], degree=poly['degree'])

# 5-against-3 with different pitches
poly = PPolymetric((5, 0), (3, 4), total=4)
d1 >> pluck(dur=poly['dur'], degree=poly['degree'])
```

**Parameters:** `*divisions` (tuples of (pulses, value)), `total` (beats, default 4)

## 6. Spatial Audio Patterns

Pattern helpers and FX for stereo/multichannel spatial movement.

### POrbit — Sine pan positions

Pre-computed sine wave positions for the `pan` attribute.

```python
# Slow circular pan (16 steps)
d1 >> pluck(pan=POrbit(0.25, 1.0, 16), dur=0.25)

d1 >> pluck(amp=POrbit(0.25, 1.0, 16), dur=0.25)

  
# Fast narrow orbit
d1 >> pluck(amp=POrbit(1.0, 0.5, 8), dur=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `speed` (rotation speed, default 0.25), `width` (stereo width, default 1.0), `steps` (resolution, default 16)

### PStereo — Map values to stereo field

Normalizes any value list to the [-width, width] stereo range.

```python
# Map scale degrees to stereo positions
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7], amp=PStereo([0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]))

# Narrow stereo field
d1 >> pluck(pan=PStereo([0, 3, 7, 5], width=0.5))
```

**Parameters:** `values` (input list), `width` (stereo width, default 1.0)

### orbit — Orbital Pan FX

Server-side circular stereo panning synced to tempo.

```python
# Slow orbit
d1 >> pluck(orbit=0.25, orbitwidth=1)

# Fast narrow circle
d1 >> pads(orbit=2, orbitwidth=0.5)

# Varying orbit speed
d1 >> pluck(orbit=linvar([0.1, 2], 16), orbitwidth=0.8, dur=1/4)
```

**Parameters:** `orbit` (speed, synced to beat_dur), `orbitwidth` (0-1, default 1)

### fspread — Frequency-dependent stereo spread

Splits audio into low/mid/high bands and pans each differently. Low stays center, highs go wide.

```python
# Wide frequency spread
d1 >> dbass(fspread=0.9, fspreadfreq=100)

# Subtle spread with low crossover
d1 >> pads(fspread=0.4, fspreadfreq=500)
```

**Parameters:** `fspread` (amount 0-1), `fspreadfreq` (crossover frequency, default 1000)

### rotate — Multichannel rotation

PanAz-based rotation for quad output systems.

```python
# Slow quad rotation
d1 >> dbass(rotate=0.25, rotwidth=1.5)

# Fast rotation
d1 >> pluck(rotate=2, rotwidth=2)
```

**Parameters:** `rotate` (speed, synced to beat_dur), `rotwidth` (focus width, default 1.5)

## 9. Cross-Player Modulation

Convenience functions for routing one player's parameters to control another.

### follow — Track another player's parameter

```python
# d2 follows d1's melody, transposed up a fifth
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 5, 7])
d2 >> bass(degree=follow(d1, 'degree', lambda x: x + 4))

# Follow octave
d2 >> pads(oct=follow(d1, 'oct'))

# Follow with inversion
d2 >> keys(degree=follow(d1, 'degree', lambda x: 7 - x))
```

**Parameters:** `target` (player), `attr` (attribute name, default "degree"), `transform` (optional lambda)

### xmod — Cross-modulation

Maps one player's attribute to another through scaling.

```python
# d1's amplitude controls d2's filter
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.5)
d2 >> pads(lpf=xmod(d1, 'amp', scale=5000, offset=20))

# Degree controls panning
d2 >> pluck(pan=xmod(d1, 'degree', scale=0.3, offset=0))

# Amplitude controls reverb amount
d2 >> keys(room=xmod(d1, 'amp', scale=0.8, offset=0.1))
```

**Parameters:** `source` (player), `attr` (default "amp"), `scale` (default 1), `offset` (default 0)

## 10. Audio-Reactive System

Real-time audio analysis from SuperCollider fed back into Python patterns.

### Setup

```python
# Start analysis on a player
reactive(d1)
d1 >> dbass()
# Stop analysis
unreactive(d1)
```

### PAmp — Amplitude follower

Pattern that tracks another player's amplitude in real-time.

```python
# d2's filter follows d1's volume
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.5)
reactive(d1)
d2 >> pads(lpf=PAmp(d1, scale=5000, smooth=0.3))

# Amplitude-driven reverb
d2 >> keys(room=PAmp(d1, scale=0.8, smooth=0.5))
```

**Parameters:** `player`, `scale` (multiplier, default 1), `smooth` (smoothing 0-1, default 0.5)

### POnset — Onset detection

Returns 1 on detected onsets, 0 otherwise.

```python
# Trigger pluck on every kick hit
d1 >> play("x", dur=1)
reactive(d1)
d2 >> pluck(amplify=POnset(d1, threshold=1.9))
```

**Parameters:** `player`, `threshold` (default 0.5)

### PReact — Custom reactive mapping

Generic audio-reactive pattern with a custom function.

```python
# Custom amplitude mapping
reactive(d1)
d2 >> pluck(degree=PReact(d1, 'amp', func=lambda x: int(x * 7)))

# Onset-triggered random
d2 >> pluck(degree=PReact(d1, 'onset', func=lambda x: PRand(0, 7)[:1] if x > 0 else 0))
```

**Parameters:** `player`, `param` ('amp' or 'onset'), `func` (mapping function)

## 11. Granular & Sample Manipulation SynthDefs

Buffer-based synths for granular processing, time-stretching, and slicing.

### grainX — Advanced granular synth

GrainBuf-based granular synthesis with fine-grained control.

```python
# Basic granular playback
d1 >> grainX("break16", pos=0.5, density=20, size=0.1, dur=4)

# Scanning through a sample
d1 >> grainX("break", pos=linvar([0, 1], 8), density=15, size=0.05)

# With slice positions
d1 >> grainX("break16", pos=slice_buf(16), dur=0.25, density=10, size=0.1)

# Spray and jitter for texture
d1 >> grainX("ambient", pos=0.3, density=30, size=0.2, spray=0.1, jitter=0.05)
```

**Parameters:** `pos` (0-1 buffer position), `density` (grains/sec, default 10), `size` (grain duration, default 0.1), `spray` (position randomness), `jitter` (timing randomness), `scan` (auto-scan), `shape` (envelope shape), `spread` (stereo spread)

### gsynth — TGrains granular synth

TGrains-based granular synthesis.

```python
# Granular texture
d1 >> gsynth("break", pos=0.5, density=10, size=0.5, dur=4)

# Pitch-shifted grains
d1 >> gsynth("break", pos=linvar([0, 1], 16), deg=0.5, density=20)

# Slice-based granular
d1 >> gsynth("break16", pos=slice_buf(8), dur=0.5, size=0.3)
```

**Parameters:** `pos` (buffer position), `density` (trigger rate, default 10), `size` (grain dur, default 0.5), `deg` (pitch ratio, default 1)

### timestretch — Warp1 time stretcher

Independent time and pitch control using Warp1.

```python
# Half-speed (double length)
d1 >> timestretch("break", stretchratio=2, sus=8)

# Double-speed
d1 >> timestretch("break", stretchratio=0.5, sus=2)

# Normal speed, smooth granular quality
d1 >> timestretch("break16
                  
                  ", stretchratio=1, windowSize=0.3, overlaps=12)

# Extreme stretch for ambient texture
d1 >> timestretch("ambient", stretchratio=8, sus=32, windowSize=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `stretchratio` (1=normal, 2=half-speed, 0.5=double-speed), `windowSize` (default 0.2), `overlaps` (quality, default 8)

### slicer — Buffer slice playback

Plays a normalized region of a buffer, automatically adjusting rate to fit the slice into `sus`.

```python
# Play first quarter of a sample
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=0, slice_end=0.25, sus=1)

# Play second half
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=0.5, slice_end=1.0, sus=2)

# Sequenced slices
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=P[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75],
                       slice_end=P[0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0], dur=0.5)

# Random slice selection
d1 >> slicer("break",
    slice_start=PRand(0, 0.75),
    slice_end=PRand(0.25, 1.0),
    dur=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `slice_start` (0-1, default 0), `slice_end` (0-1, default 1)

### tstretch — Time stretch FX

PitchShift-based time manipulation applied as an effect on any synth. Preserves pitch.

```python
# Subtle time smear on a synth
d1 >> pluck(dur=0.5, tstretch=0.8, tstretchsize=1.0)

# Heavy granular processing
d1 >> bass(dur=1, tstretch=0.2, tstretchsize=0.1)

# Varying stretch amount
d1 >> pads(dur=2, tstretch=linvar([0.5, 2], 8))
```

**Parameters:** `tstretch` (ratio, 1=bypass), `tstretchsize` (grain window, default 0.2)

### Other sample SynthDefs

d1 >> loop("break", beat_stretch=1, dur=4)

# No-loop (one-shot)

## 12. Live Looping

Real-time recording and looping system with overdub support.

### Basic usage

```python
# Create a 4-beat loop buffer
ll = LiveLooper(duration=4)
                  
                  

# Record from hardware input
ll.rec()                      # starts at next bar
ll.stop_rec()                 # stop recording

# Play back
d1 >> ll.play(beat_stretch=1, room=0.3)

# Overdub at 50% blend
ll.overdub(amount=0.5)
ll.stop_rec()
```

### Capture from another player

```python
# Record d1's output
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 7], dur=0.5)
ll = LiveLooper(duration=8)
ll.from_player(d1)            # capture d1's audio
ll.stop_rec()
d2 >> ll.play(beat_stretch=1)
```

### Multiple loopers

```python
# Layer multiple loops
ll1 = LiveLooper(duration=4)
ll2 = LiveLooper(duration=8)

ll1.rec(channel=0)           # record from input channel 0
ll2.rec(channel=1)           # record from input channel 1

# Play both
d1 >> ll1.play(beat_stretch=1)
d2 >> ll2.play(beat_stretch=1, room=0.5)
```

### Cleanup

```python
ll.free()                     # stop recording and free buffer
```

## 14. Audio Effects Reference

All effects are applied as keyword arguments on any player. Organized by category.

### Envelope
d1 >> pluck(a=0.5, ac=3, rc=-1, position=0.3)
                  
| Parameter | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `leg=N` | Legato slide (XLine scaling) | `d1 >> pluck(leg=0.5)` |
| `a=T, ac=C` | Attack time with curve | `d1 >> pluck(a=0.5, ac=-3)` |
| `r=T, rc=C` | Release time with curve | `d1 >> pluck(r=0.5, rc=-3)` |
| `position=P` | Trim: silence before position (0-1 of sus) | `d1 >> pluck(position=0.5)` |
| `transient=T, transattack=A, transsustain=S` | Transient shaper | `d1 >> play("x", transient=0.8, transattack=2)` |
| `drift=D, driftspeed=S, driftdepth=D` | Humanized timing drift | `d1 >> pluck(drift=0.5, driftspeed=2)` |

### Pitch
                  
d1 >> pluck(fshift=100, fmix=0.1)
d1 >> pluck(glide=2, glidedur=0.1)
| Parameter | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `glide=G, glidedur=D` | Portamento from G*freq to freq | `d1 >> pluck(glide=2, glidedur=0.1)` |
| `glide2=S, glide2dur=D` | Semitone glissando over sus | `d1 >> pluck(glide2=7, glide2dur=0.5)` |
| `octer=O, octersub=S, octersubsub=SS` | Octave up + sub-octaves | `d1 >> pluck(octer=0.5, octersub=0.3)` |
| `shift=S, shiftsize=W` | PitchShift.ar pitch shift | `d1 >> pluck(shift=7, shiftsize=0.1)` |
| `fshift=Hz, fphase=P, fmix=M` | Fixed Hz frequency shift | `d1 >> pluck(fshift=100, fmix=0.5)` |
| `blow=B, bflow=F, bmodel=M, bpos=P` | MiBlow resonator | `d1 >> pluck(blow=0.5, bflow=0.5)` |

### Filter

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `spf=F, spr=R, spfslide=S, spfend=E` | Sliding RLPF | `d1 >> pluck(spf=200, spfend=8000, spfslide=0.5)` |

## 15. Modulation & Envelope System

A unified system for parameter modulation combining Python-side pattern generators, helper functions for FoxDot's built-in auto-control system, and new SC-side modulation FX.

### Hidden Auto-Control System

FoxDot auto-generates control signals for every FX parameter. For any parameter `param`, you get:

- `param_` — target value for `Line.kr` ramp
- `param_d` — ramp duration
- `paramlfo` — SinOsc.kr rate
- `paramlfomul` — LFO multiply
- `paramlfoadd` — LFO add

```python
# Manual usage: ramp lpf from 200 to 8000 over 0.5 beats
d1 >> pluck(lpf=200, lpf_=8000, lpf_d=0.5)

# Add sine LFO to lpf
d1 >> pluck(lpf=2000, lpflfo=4, lpflfomul=0.5, lpflfoadd=1)
```

### Helper Functions: ramp(), lfo(), mod()

Convenience functions that return dicts for `**kwargs` unpacking.

#### `ramp(param, start, end, dur=1)`

d1 >> pluck(**ramp('lpf', 200, 8000, dur=0.5))
            
```python
# Ramp filter from 200 to 8000 over 0.5 beats
d1 >> pluck(**ramp('lpf', 200, 8000, dur=0.5))

# Ramp pan from left to right
d1 >> pluck(**ramp('pan', -1, 1, dur=2))
```

#### `lfo(param, rate, mul=1, add=1)`

```python
# Sine LFO on filter at 4Hz
d1 >> pluck(lpf=4000, **lfo('lpf', rate=4, mul=0.5))

# Vibrato via LFO on pitch
d1 >> pluck(**lfo('pitch', rate=1, mul=0.53))
```

#### `mod(param, start=None, end=None, dur=1, rate=0, mul=1, add=1)`

Combined ramp + LFO in one call.

```python
# Filter sweep with wobble
d1 >> pluck(**mod('lpf', start=200, end=8000, rate=4, mul=0.2))

# Just LFO, no ramp
d1 >> pluck(lpf=2000, **mod('lpf', rate=8, mul=0.3))
```

### Pattern Generators

#### `PEnv(levels, times, curve, steps)` — Multi-segment envelope

```python
# ADSR-like filter sweep
d1 >> pluck(lpf=PEnv([200, 8000, 2000, 200], [0.2, 0.5, 0.3], curve=-4, steps=32), dur=1/32)

# Exponential envelope
d1 >> pluck(amp=PEnv([0, 1, 0], curve='exp', steps=16), dur=1/16)

# Sine-curved attack
d1 >> pads(lpf=PEnv([200, 8000, 4000], [0.3, 0.7], curve='sin', steps=64), dur=1/64)
```

**Parameters:**
| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `levels` | (required) | Breakpoint values, e.g. `[0, 1, 0.5, 0]` |
| `times` | `None` | Relative segment durations (auto-equal if None) |
| `curve` | `'lin'` | `'lin'`, `'exp'`, `'sin'`, or numeric (-4 = fast ease-out) |
| `steps` | `16` | Total output values |

#### `PLFO(shape, rate, depth, center, steps)` — LFO waveform

```python
# Triangle pan sweep
d1 >> pluck(pan=PLFO('tri', rate=1, depth=1, steps=16), dur=1/16)

# Square wave gate
d1 >> pluck(amp=PLFO('square', rate=2, depth=0.5, center=0.5, steps=16), dur=1/16)

# Saw ramp on filter
d1 >> bass(lpf=PLFO('saw', rate=1, depth=3000, center=3000, steps=32), dur=1/32)

# Random modulation
d1 >> pluck(pan=PLFO('noise', rate=1, depth=1, steps=16), dur=1/16)
```

**Parameters:**
| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `shape` | `'sin'` | `'sin'`, `'tri'`, `'saw'`, `'square'`, `'noise'` |
| `rate` | `1` | Cycles within the step count |
| `depth` | `1` | Amplitude of waveform |
| `center` | `0` | DC offset |
| `steps` | `16` | Total output values |

#### `PRamp(start, end, steps)` — Linear ramp

```python
d1 >> pluck(lpf=PRamp(200, 8000, 16), dur=1/16)
d1 >> pluck(pan=PRamp(-1, 1, 8), dur=0.5)
```

#### `PStep(values, holds)` — Step sequencer

```python
# Each value held for 4 steps
d1 >> pluck(hpf=PStep([200, 800, 400, 1200], holds=[4, 4, 4, 4]), dur=1/16)

# Default: 1 step each
d1 >> pluck(degree=PStep([0, 4, 7, 12]))
```

### SC-side Modulation FX

#### `envmod` — ADSR Amplitude Modulator

Applies an ADSR envelope to the signal amplitude. Crossfades with dry signal via the `envmod` parameter.

```python
# Standard ADSR envelope
d1 >> pluck(envmod=1, ematk=0.01, emdec=0.2, emslev=0.6, emrel=0.3)

# Slow pad swell
d1 >> pads(envmod=1, ematk=0.5, emdec=0.3, emslev=0.8, emrel=0.5)

# Partial envelope blend
d1 >> pluck(envmod=0.5, ematk=0.1, emdec=0.4, emslev=0.3, emrel=0.1)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `envmod` | `0` | Dry/wet (0=bypass, 1=full envelope) |
| `ematk` | `0.01` | Attack time (fraction of sus) |
| `emdec` | `0.3` | Decay time (fraction of sus) |
| `emslev` | `0.7` | Sustain level (0-1) |
| `emrel` | `0.2` | Release time (fraction of sus) |
| `emcurve` | `-4` | Envelope curve (negative=fast decay) |

#### `envfilt` — ADSR Envelope Filter

ADSR-shaped filter sweep with selectable filter type.

```python
# Acid bass (fast attack, short decay)
d1 >> bass(envfilt=1, efstart=200, efpeak=6000, efattk=0.01, efdec=0.3, efsus=0.2, efres=0.3)

# Slow filter sweep
d1 >> pads(envfilt=1, efstart=500, efpeak=12000, efattk=0.3, efdec=0.5, efsus=0.6, efres=0.5)

# HPF envelope (eftype=1)
d1 >> pluck(envfilt=1, eftype=1, efstart=100, efpeak=4000, efdec=0.5)

# BPF envelope (eftype=2)
d1 >> pads(envfilt=0.8, eftype=2, efstart=300, efpeak=3000, efres=0.1)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `envfilt` | `0` | Dry/wet |
| `efstart` | `200` | Start frequency |
| `efpeak` | `8000` | Peak frequency |
| `efattk` | `0.01` | Attack time |
| `efdec` | `0.3` | Decay time |
| `efsus` | `0.5` | Sustain level (0-1, interpolates start↔peak) |
| `efrel` | `0.2` | Release time |
| `efcurve` | `-4` | Curve shape |
| `efres` | `0.5` | Filter resonance |
| `eftype` | `0` | 0=LPF, 1=HPF, 2=BPF |

#### `lfomod` — Multi-Shape LFO Amplitude Modulator

LFO-driven tremolo with 6 waveform shapes and optional beat sync.

```python
# Sine tremolo
d1 >> pluck(lfomod=-0.6, lmrate=1)

# Triangle, beat-synced
d1 >> pluck(lfomod=0.8, lmrate=4, lmshape=1, lmsync=1)

# Square gate
d1 >> pads(lfomod=1, lmrate=8, lmshape=3)

# Smooth random modulation
d1 >> pluck(lfomod=0.5, lmrate=2
            , lmshape=4)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `lfomod` | `0` | Dry/wet (depth) |
| `lmrate` | `4` | LFO rate (Hz, or beats if synced) |
| `lmshape` | `0` | 0=sin, 1=tri, 2=saw, 3=pulse, 4=smooth noise, 5=S&H |
| `lmphase` | `0` | LFO starting phase |
| `lmsync` | `0` | 0=free Hz, 1=beat-synced |

#### `lfofilt` — Multi-Shape LFO Filter

LFO-controlled filter with selectable waveform and filter type.

```python
# Auto-wah (sine LFO)
d1 >> bass(lfofilt=1, lfcenter=1500, lfdepth=1200, lfrate=2, lfres=0.3)

# Saw sweep filter
d1 >> pads(lfofilt=1, lfcenter=3000, lfdepth=2000, lfrate=1, lfshape=2)

# Beat-synced triangle filter
d1 >> pluck(lfofilt=1, lfcenter=2000, lfdepth=1500, lfrate=4, lfshape=1, lfsync=1)

# Random filter with HPF
d1 >> bass(lfofilt=0.7, lftype=1, lfcenter=1000, lfdepth=800, lfrate=3, lfshape=4)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `lfofilt` | `0` | Dry/wet |
| `lfcenter` | `2000` | Center frequency |
| `lfdepth` | `1500` | LFO depth in Hz |
| `lfrate` | `2` | LFO rate |
| `lfshape` | `0` | 0=sin, 1=tri, 2=saw, 3=pulse, 4=smooth noise, 5=S&H |
| `lfres` | `0.5` | Filter resonance |
| `lftype` | `0` | 0=LPF, 1=HPF, 2=BPF |
| `lfsync` | `0` | 0=free Hz, 1=beat-synced |

#### `vocoder` — Band Vocoder

8-band vocoder that imposes the spectral envelope of the input onto a carrier oscillator.

```python
# Classic vocoder with saw carrier
d1 >> pads(vocoder=0.7, vocfreq=100, vocq=0.03)

# Pulse carrier for buzzy tone
d1 >> pads(vocoder=0.8, voccarrier=1, vocfreq=80)

# Noise carrier for whisper effect
d1 >> pads(vocoder=0.6, voccarrier=2, vocq=0.05)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `vocoder` | `0` | Dry/wet |
| `voccarrier` | `0` | 0=saw, 1=pulse, 2=noise |
| `vocfreq` | `100` | Carrier base frequency |

## 1. Generative Patterns

Algorithmic pattern generators that produce evolving, non-repeating sequences.

### PMarkov2 — Higher-order Markov chain

Analyzes an input sequence and builds N-gram transition tables. Falls back to shorter context windows when no exact match is found.

```python
# Train on a melody, generate new notes in the same style
d1 >> pluck(degree=[0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 5, 4, 2], dur=0.5)

# Order 1 = more random, order 3 = closer to source
d1 >> pluck(degree=PMarkov2([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1], order=9), dur=1/4)

# Use with scale degrees for generative melodies
d1 >> keys(degree=PMarkov2([0, 2, 4, 7, 9, 7, 4, 2, 0], order=3), sus=2, dur=1)
```

**Parameters:** `data` (source sequence), `order` (N-gram depth, default 2)

### PLife — Cellular automaton

1D elementary cellular automaton (Wolfram Rules 30, 90, 110, etc.) mapped to 0/1 values. Useful for binary rhythms and gates.

```python
# Rule 30 rhythm (chaotic)
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=30, size=16))

# Rule 110 (complex) as degree selection
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLife(rule=110, size=8) * 7, dur=0.5)

# Combine rules for layered rhythms
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=30, size=32))
d2 >> play("o", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=90, size=32))
```

**Parameters:** `rule` (rule number, default 30), `size` (grid width, default 16), `row` (starting row, default 0)

### PLSystem — L-system rewriting

L-system string rewriting mapped to numeric values. Default is Fibonacci L-system.

```python
# Default Fibonacci L-system
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLSystem(), dur=0.5)

# Custom L-system with custom mapping
d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PLSystem(
        axiom="A",
        rules={"A": "AB", "B": "A"},
        generations=8,
        mapping={"A": 0, "B": 4}
    ),
    dur=0.25
)

# Plant-like branching pattern
d1 >> keys(
    degree=PLSystem(axiom="F", rules={"F": "F+F-F"}, generations=4,
                    mapping={"F": 0, "+": 3, "-": -2}),
    dur=0.5, sus=2
)
```

**Parameters:** `axiom` (start string), `rules` (rewrite dict), `generations` (default 6), `mapping` (char-to-value dict)

### PEvolve — Genetic algorithm

Maintains a population of sequences, selects via tournament, crosses over, mutates, and walks through individuals.

```python
# Evolve a melody toward consonance
  
def consonance(seq):
    return sum(1 for x in seq if x in [0, 2, 4, 5, 7])

d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PEvolve([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], fitness=consonance, mutation=0.3),
    dur=0.5
)

# Evolve rhythmic density
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25,
    amplify=PEvolve([1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1],
                     fitness=lambda s: -abs(sum(s) - 5),  # target 5 hits
                     mutation=0.15))
```

**Parameters:** `population` (source values), `fitness` (fitness function), `mutation` (rate, default 0.1), `crossover` (rate, default 0.7), `pop_size` (default 8)

## 2. Stochastic Patterns

Probability-based and noise generators for humanization and controlled randomness.

### PGauss — Gaussian distribution

```python
# Humanized timing (slight random delay)
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.5, delay=PGauss(mean=0, sigma=0.02))

# Pitch variation around a center note
d1 >> pluck(degree=PGauss(4, 1), dur=0.5)

# Random velocity with normal distribution
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PGauss(mean=0.7, sigma=0.15))
```

**Parameters:** `mean` (center, default 0), `sigma` (std deviation, default 1)

### PBrown — Brownian motion

Constrained random walk. Each step adds a gaussian offset clamped to [lo, hi].

```python
# Drifting filter cutoff
d1 >> pluck(dur=0.5, lpf=PBrown(lo=200, hi=4000, step=100))

# Wandering pitch
d1 >> sine(degree=PBrown(lo=0, hi=7, step=1), dur=0.25)

# Slow panning drift
d1 >> pads(dur=2, pan=PBrown(lo=-1, hi=1, step=0.2))
```

**Parameters:** `lo` (lower bound, default 0), `hi` (upper bound, default 1), `step` (step size, default 0.1)

### PLogistic — Chaotic map

Logistic map: `x = r*x*(1-x)`. Produces chaos near r=3.9-4.0.

```python
# Chaotic pitch sequence
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLogistic(r=3.60, scale=1), dur=0.25)

# Edge of chaos (r=3.57 = period doubling)
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLogistic(r=3.57, scale=12, offset=-6), dur=0.5)

# Chaotic rhythm density
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLogistic(r=3.5, scale=1))
```

**Parameters:** `r` (growth rate, default 3.9), `x0` (initial value, default 0.5), `scale` (output scale, default 1), `offset` (default 0)

### PSkip — Probability gate

Passes source values with a given probability, otherwise returns a default value.

```python
# Sparse hi-hat pattern (50% chance of playing)
d1 >> play("-", dur=0.25, amplify=PSkip(P[1], prob=0.5, default=0))

# Random note omission
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 5, 7], dur=0.5,
            amplify=PSkip(P[1], prob=0.7, default=0))

# Ghost notes on snare
d2 >> play("o", dur=0.5, amplify=PSkip(P[0.3], prob=0.4, default=0))
```

**Parameters:** `pattern` (source), `prob` (probability, default 0.5), `default` (fallback value, default 0)

### PSwitch — Weighted pattern switching

Each step randomly selects one of the source patterns based on weights.

```python
# Switch between two melodies
d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PSwitch([P[0, 2, 4], P[5, 7, 9]], weights=[0.7, 0.3]),
    dur=0.5
)

# Weighted rhythm switching
d1 >> play(
    PSwitch([P["x o x o"], P["x x . x"], P["x . x ."]], weights=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2]),
    dur=0.25
)
```

**Parameters:** `patterns` (list of patterns), `weights` (selection weights, default equal)

Pre-built swing, groove, and accent patterns from classic hardware.

### PSwing — Swing delay

```python
# Basic swing feel
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.25, delay=PSwing(0.1))

# Heavy swing
d1 >> play("x-o-", dur=0.25, delay=PSwing(0.4))
```

**Parameters:** `amount` (swing amount, default 0.1), `steps` (default 8)

### PGroove — Named groove templates

Available grooves: `mpc60`, `tr808`, `sp1200`, `linn`, `shuffle`, `clave`

```python
# MPC-60 feel
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("mpc60"))

# TR-808 groove
d1 >> play("x-o-x-o-", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("tr808", steps=16))

# SP-1200 timing
d1 >> play("xo", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("sp1200"))

# Clave groove
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, delay=PGroove("clave", steps=16))
```

**Parameters:** `name` (template name), `steps` (default 16)

### PAccent — Velocity accent patterns

Available accents: `backbeat`, `four_floor`, `offbeat`, `ghost`

```python
# Backbeat accents (snare on 2 and 4)
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PAccent("backbeat", steps=16))

d2 >> dbass(amp=PAccent("backbeat", steps=16), dur=1/4)  
  
# Four-on-the-floor kick emphasis
d1 >> play("V", dur=0.25, amplify=PAccent("four_floor", steps=32))

# Ghost note pattern

# Combine groove + accent

           delay=PGroove("mpc60"),
           amplify=PAccent("backbeat"))
```

**Parameters:** `name` (template name), `steps` (default 16)

## 4. Advanced Euclidean Rhythms

Extensions to the built-in PEuclid for more complex rhythmic structures.

### PEuclidR — Rotated Euclidean

```python
# Standard Euclidean: 5 hits in 8 steps
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclid(5, 8))

d2 >> play("o", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidR(5, 8, rotation=2))


**Parameters:** `n` (pulses), `k` (steps), `rotation` (default 1)

### PEuclidFill — Layered Euclidean

OR-combines multiple Euclidean rhythms. Returns 1 where any layer has a pulse.

```python
# Layer 3-in-8 and 5-in-8
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidFill((3, 8), ([9, 3], 12)))

# Dense polyrhythmic fill
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amp=1,amplify=PEuclidFill((3, 16), (5, 8), (7, 16)))
```

**Parameters:** `*pairs` (tuples of (n, k) — all must share the same k)

### PEuclidAccent — Euclidean with accents

Two-layer Euclidean: base hits + accent layer. Returns 0 (rest), 0.5 (normal), or 1.0 (accent).

```python
# 5-in-8 with accented subset
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidAccent(5, 8, accent_n=2))

# 7-in-16 with 3 accents
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidAccent(7, 16, accent_n=3))
```

**Parameters:** `n`, `k`, `accent_n` (default n//2), `accent_k` (default k)

## 5. Polymetric Tools

Duration pattern helpers for tuplets and metric divisions.

### PMetric — N pulses in M beats

```python
# 5 evenly-spaced notes in 4 beats
d1 >> pluck(dur=PMetric(5, 4))

# 7 notes in 2 beats
d2 >> bass(dur=PMetric(7, 2))

# 3 in 1 beat (= triplet)
d3 >> keys(dur=PMetric(3, 1))
```

**Parameters:** `pulses`, `period` (default 1)

### PTriplet — Triplet shorthand

```python
# Triplets against quarter notes
d1 >> pluck(dur=1)
d2 >> pluck(dur=PTriplet(1), oct=5)

# Half-note triplets
d3 >> bass(dur=PTriplet(2))
```

**Parameters:** `dur` (default 1)

### PQuintuplet — Quintuplet shorthand

```python
# 5 notes in 2 beats
d1 >> pluck(dur=PQuintuplet(2))

# 5 in 1 beat
d2 >> pluck(dur=PQuintuplet(1), oct=5)
```

**Parameters:** `dur` (default 1)

### PPolymetric — Merged polymetric timeline

Merges multiple (pulses, value) pairs into a single interleaved timeline. Returns a dict with `dur` and `degree` patterns.

```python
# 3-against-4 polyrhythm
poly = PPolymetric((3, 0), (4, 2), total=4)
d1 >> pluck(dur=poly['dur'], degree=poly['degree'])

# 5-against-3 with different pitches
poly = PPolymetric((5, 0), (3, 4), total=4)
d1 >> pluck(dur=poly['dur'], degree=poly['degree'])
```

**Parameters:** `*divisions` (tuples of (pulses, value)), `total` (beats, default 4)

## 6. Spatial Audio Patterns

Pattern helpers and FX for stereo/multichannel spatial movement.

### POrbit — Sine pan positions

Pre-computed sine wave positions for the `pan` attribute.

```python
# Slow circular pan (16 steps)
d1 >> pluck(pan=POrbit(0.25, 1.0, 16), dur=0.25)

d1 >> pluck(amp=POrbit(0.25, 1.0, 16), dur=0.25)

  
# Fast narrow orbit
d1 >> pluck(amp=POrbit(1.0, 0.5, 8), dur=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `speed` (rotation speed, default 0.25), `width` (stereo width, default 1.0), `steps` (resolution, default 16)

### PStereo — Map values to stereo field

Normalizes any value list to the [-width, width] stereo range.

```python
# Map scale degrees to stereo positions
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7], amp=PStereo([0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]))

# Narrow stereo field
d1 >> pluck(pan=PStereo([0, 3, 7, 5], width=0.5))
```

**Parameters:** `values` (input list), `width` (stereo width, default 1.0)

### orbit — Orbital Pan FX

Server-side circular stereo panning synced to tempo.

```python
# Slow orbit
d1 >> pluck(orbit=0.25, orbitwidth=1)

# Fast narrow circle
d1 >> pads(orbit=2, orbitwidth=0.5)

# Varying orbit speed
d1 >> pluck(orbit=linvar([0.1, 2], 16), orbitwidth=0.8, dur=1/4)
```

**Parameters:** `orbit` (speed, synced to beat_dur), `orbitwidth` (0-1, default 1)

### fspread — Frequency-dependent stereo spread

Splits audio into low/mid/high bands and pans each differently. Low stays center, highs go wide.

```python
# Wide frequency spread
d1 >> dbass(fspread=0.9, fspreadfreq=100)

# Subtle spread with low crossover
d1 >> pads(fspread=0.4, fspreadfreq=500)
```

**Parameters:** `fspread` (amount 0-1), `fspreadfreq` (crossover frequency, default 1000)

### rotate — Multichannel rotation

PanAz-based rotation for quad output systems.

```python
# Slow quad rotation
d1 >> dbass(rotate=0.25, rotwidth=1.5)

# Fast rotation
d1 >> pluck(rotate=2, rotwidth=2)
```

**Parameters:** `rotate` (speed, synced to beat_dur), `rotwidth` (focus width, default 1.5)

## 9. Cross-Player Modulation

Convenience functions for routing one player's parameters to control another.

### follow — Track another player's parameter

```python
# d2 follows d1's melody, transposed up a fifth
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 5, 7])
d2 >> bass(degree=follow(d1, 'degree', lambda x: x + 4))

# Follow octave
d2 >> pads(oct=follow(d1, 'oct'))

# Follow with inversion
d2 >> keys(degree=follow(d1, 'degree', lambda x: 7 - x))
```

Maps one player's attribute to another through scaling.

d2 >> pluck(pan=xmod(d1, 'degree', scale=0.3, offset=0))

# Amplitude controls reverb amount

```

**Parameters:** `source` (player), `attr` (default "amp"), `scale` (default 1), `offset` (default 0)

## 10. Audio-Reactive System

Real-time audio analysis from SuperCollider fed back into Python patterns.

### Setup

```python
# Start analysis on a player
reactive(d1)
d1 >> dbass()
# Stop analysis
unreactive(d1)
```

### PAmp — Amplitude follower

Pattern that tracks another player's amplitude in real-time.

```python
# d2's filter follows d1's volume
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.5)
reactive(d1)
d2 >> pads(lpf=PAmp(d1, scale=5000, smooth=0.3))

# Amplitude-driven reverb
d2 >> keys(room=PAmp(d1, scale=0.8, smooth=0.5))
```

**Parameters:** `player`, `scale` (multiplier, default 1), `smooth` (smoothing 0-1, default 0.5)

### POnset — Onset detection

Returns 1 on detected onsets, 0 otherwise.

```python
# Trigger pluck on every kick hit
d1 >> play("x", dur=1)
reactive(d1)
d2 >> pluck(amplify=POnset(d1, threshold=1.9))
```

**Parameters:** `player`, `threshold` (default 0.5)

### PReact — Custom reactive mapping

Generic audio-reactive pattern with a custom function.

```python
# Custom amplitude mapping
reactive(d1)
d2 >> pluck(degree=PReact(d1, 'amp', func=lambda x: int(x * 7)))

# Onset-triggered random
d2 >> pluck(degree=PReact(d1, 'onset', func=lambda x: PRand(0, 7)[:1] if x > 0 else 0))
```

**Parameters:** `player`, `param` ('amp' or 'onset'), `func` (mapping function)

## 11. Granular & Sample Manipulation SynthDefs

Buffer-based synths for granular processing, time-stretching, and slicing.

### grainX — Advanced granular synth

GrainBuf-based granular synthesis with fine-grained control.

```python
# Basic granular playback
d1 >> grainX("break16", pos=0.5, density=20, size=0.1, dur=4)

# Scanning through a sample
d1 >> grainX("break", pos=linvar([0, 1], 8), density=15, size=0.05)

# With slice positions
d1 >> grainX("break16", pos=slice_buf(16), dur=0.25, density=10, size=0.1)

# Spray and jitter for texture
d1 >> grainX("ambient", pos=0.3, density=30, size=0.2, spray=0.1, jitter=0.05)
```

**Parameters:** `pos` (0-1 buffer position), `density` (grains/sec, default 10), `size` (grain duration, default 0.1), `spray` (position randomness), `jitter` (timing randomness), `scan` (auto-scan), `shape` (envelope shape), `spread` (stereo spread)

### gsynth — TGrains granular synth

TGrains-based granular synthesis.

```python
# Granular texture
d1 >> gsynth("break", pos=0.5, density=10, size=0.5, dur=4)

# Pitch-shifted grains
d1 >> gsynth("break", pos=linvar([0, 1], 16), deg=0.5, density=20)

# Slice-based granular
d1 >> gsynth("break16", pos=slice_buf(8), dur=0.5, size=0.3)
```

**Parameters:** `pos` (buffer position), `density` (trigger rate, default 10), `size` (grain dur, default 0.5), `deg` (pitch ratio, default 1)

### timestretch — Warp1 time stretcher

Independent time and pitch control using Warp1.

```python
# Half-speed (double length)
d1 >> timestretch("break", stretchratio=2, sus=8)

# Double-speed
d1 >> timestretch("break", stretchratio=0.5, sus=2)

# Normal speed, smooth granular quality
d1 >> timestretch("break16
                  
                  ", stretchratio=1, windowSize=0.3, overlaps=12)

# Extreme stretch for ambient texture
d1 >> timestretch("ambient", stretchratio=8, sus=32, windowSize=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `stretchratio` (1=normal, 2=half-speed, 0.5=double-speed), `windowSize` (default 0.2), `overlaps` (quality, default 8)

### slicer — Buffer slice playback

Plays a normalized region of a buffer, automatically adjusting rate to fit the slice into `sus`.

```python
# Play first quarter of a sample
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=0, slice_end=0.25, sus=1)

# Play second half
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=0.5, slice_end=1.0, sus=2)

# Sequenced slices
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=P[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75],
                       slice_end=P[0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0], dur=0.5)

# Random slice selection
d1 >> slicer("break",
    slice_start=PRand(0, 0.75),
    slice_end=PRand(0.25, 1.0),
    dur=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `slice_start` (0-1, default 0), `slice_end` (0-1, default 1)

### tstretch — Time stretch FX

PitchShift-based time manipulation applied as an effect on any synth. Preserves pitch.

```python
# Subtle time smear on a synth
d1 >> pluck(dur=0.5, tstretch=0.8, tstretchsize=1.0)

# Heavy granular processing
d1 >> bass(dur=1, tstretch=0.2, tstretchsize=0.1)

# Varying stretch amount
d1 >> pads(dur=2, tstretch=linvar([0.5, 2], 8))
```

**Parameters:** `tstretch` (ratio, 1=bypass), `tstretchsize` (grain window, default 0.2)

## 12. Live Looping

Real-time recording and looping system with overdub support.

### Basic usage

```python
# Create a 4-beat loop buffer
ll = LiveLooper(duration=4)
                  
                  

# Record from hardware input
ll.rec()                      # starts at next bar
ll.stop_rec()                 # stop recording

# Play back
d1 >> ll.play(beat_stretch=1, room=0.3)

# Overdub at 50% blend
ll.overdub(amount=0.5)
ll.stop_rec()
```

### Capture from another player

```python
# Record d1's output
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 7], dur=0.5)
ll = LiveLooper(duration=8)
ll.from_player(d1)            # capture d1's audio
ll.stop_rec()
d2 >> ll.play(beat_stretch=1)
```

### Multiple loopers

```python
# Layer multiple loops
ll1 = LiveLooper(duration=4)
ll2 = LiveLooper(duration=8)

ll1.rec(channel=0)           # record from input channel 0
ll2.rec(channel=1)           # record from input channel 1

# Play both
d1 >> ll1.play(beat_stretch=1)
d2 >> ll2.play(beat_stretch=1, room=0.5)
```

### Cleanup

```python
ll.free()                     # stop recording and free buffer
```

## 14. Audio Effects Reference

All effects are applied as keyword arguments on any player. Organized by category.

### Envelope
d1 >> pluck(a=0.5, ac=3, rc=-1, position=0.3)
                  
| Parameter | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `leg=N` | Legato slide (XLine scaling) | `d1 >> pluck(leg=0.5)` |
| `a=T, ac=C` | Attack time with curve | `d1 >> pluck(a=0.5, ac=-3)` |
| `r=T, rc=C` | Release time with curve | `d1 >> pluck(r=0.5, rc=-3)` |
| `position=P` | Trim: silence before position (0-1 of sus) | `d1 >> pluck(position=0.5)` |
| `transient=T, transattack=A, transsustain=S` | Transient shaper | `d1 >> play("x", transient=0.8, transattack=2)` |
| `drift=D, driftspeed=S, driftdepth=D` | Humanized timing drift | `d1 >> pluck(drift=0.5, driftspeed=2)` |

### Pitch
                  
d1 >> pluck(fshift=100, fmix=0.1)
d1 >> pluck(glide=2, glidedur=0.1)
| Parameter | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `glide=G, glidedur=D` | Portamento from G*freq to freq | `d1 >> pluck(glide=2, glidedur=0.1)` |
| `glide2=S, glide2dur=D` | Semitone glissando over sus | `d1 >> pluck(glide2=7, glide2dur=0.5)` |
| `octer=O, octersub=S, octersubsub=SS` | Octave up + sub-octaves | `d1 >> pluck(octer=0.5, octersub=0.3)` |
| `shift=S, shiftsize=W` | PitchShift.ar pitch shift | `d1 >> pluck(shift=7, shiftsize=0.1)` |
| `fshift=Hz, fphase=P, fmix=M` | Fixed Hz frequency shift | `d1 >> pluck(fshift=100, fmix=0.5)` |
| `blow=B, bflow=F, bmodel=M, bpos=P` | MiBlow resonator | `d1 >> pluck(blow=0.5, bflow=0.5)` |

### Filter

## 15. Modulation & Envelope System

A unified system for parameter modulation combining Python-side pattern generators, helper functions for FoxDot's built-in auto-control system, and new SC-side modulation FX.

### Hidden Auto-Control System

FoxDot auto-generates control signals for every FX parameter. For any parameter `param`, you get:

- `param_` — target value for `Line.kr` ramp
- `param_d` — ramp duration
- `paramlfo` — SinOsc.kr rate
- `paramlfomul` — LFO multiply
- `paramlfoadd` — LFO add

```python
# Manual usage: ramp lpf from 200 to 8000 over 0.5 beats
d1 >> pluck(lpf=200, lpf_=8000, lpf_d=0.5)

# Add sine LFO to lpf
d1 >> pluck(lpf=2000, lpflfo=4, lpflfomul=0.5, lpflfoadd=1)
```

### Helper Functions: ramp(), lfo(), mod()

Convenience functions that return dicts for `**kwargs` unpacking.

#### `ramp(param, start, end, dur=1)`

d1 >> pluck(**ramp('lpf', 200, 8000, dur=0.5))
            
```python
# Ramp filter from 200 to 8000 over 0.5 beats
d1 >> pluck(**ramp('lpf', 200, 8000, dur=0.5))

# Ramp pan from left to right
d1 >> pluck(**ramp('pan', -1, 1, dur=2))
```

#### `lfo(param, rate, mul=1, add=1)`

```python
# Sine LFO on filter at 4Hz
d1 >> pluck(lpf=4000, **lfo('lpf', rate=4, mul=0.5))

# Vibrato via LFO on pitch
d1 >> pluck(**lfo('pitch', rate=1, mul=0.53))
```

#### `mod(param, start=None, end=None, dur=1, rate=0, mul=1, add=1)`

Combined ramp + LFO in one call.

```python
# Filter sweep with wobble
d1 >> pluck(**mod('lpf', start=200, end=8000, rate=4, mul=0.2))

# Just LFO, no ramp
d1 >> pluck(lpf=2000, **mod('lpf', rate=8, mul=0.3))
```

### Pattern Generators

#### `PEnv(levels, times, curve, steps)` — Multi-segment envelope

```python
# ADSR-like filter sweep
d1 >> pluck(lpf=PEnv([200, 8000, 2000, 200], [0.2, 0.5, 0.3], curve=-4, steps=32), dur=1/32)

# Exponential envelope
d1 >> pluck(amp=PEnv([0, 1, 0], curve='exp', steps=16), dur=1/16)

# Sine-curved attack
d1 >> pads(lpf=PEnv([200, 8000, 4000], [0.3, 0.7], curve='sin', steps=64), dur=1/64)
```

**Parameters:**
| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `levels` | (required) | Breakpoint values, e.g. `[0, 1, 0.5, 0]` |
| `times` | `None` | Relative segment durations (auto-equal if None) |
| `curve` | `'lin'` | `'lin'`, `'exp'`, `'sin'`, or numeric (-4 = fast ease-out) |
| `steps` | `16` | Total output values |

#### `PLFO(shape, rate, depth, center, steps)` — LFO waveform

```python
# Triangle pan sweep
d1 >> pluck(pan=PLFO('tri', rate=1, depth=1, steps=16), dur=1/16)

# Square wave gate
d1 >> pluck(amp=PLFO('square', rate=2, depth=0.5, center=0.5, steps=16), dur=1/16)

# Saw ramp on filter
d1 >> bass(lpf=PLFO('saw', rate=1, depth=3000, center=3000, steps=32), dur=1/32)

# Random modulation
d1 >> pluck(pan=PLFO('noise', rate=1, depth=1, steps=16), dur=1/16)
```

**Parameters:**
| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `shape` | `'sin'` | `'sin'`, `'tri'`, `'saw'`, `'square'`, `'noise'` |
| `rate` | `1` | Cycles within the step count |
| `depth` | `1` | Amplitude of waveform |
| `center` | `0` | DC offset |
| `steps` | `16` | Total output values |

#### `PRamp(start, end, steps)` — Linear ramp

```python
d1 >> pluck(lpf=PRamp(200, 8000, 16), dur=1/16)
d1 >> pluck(pan=PRamp(-1, 1, 8), dur=0.5)
```

#### `PStep(values, holds)` — Step sequencer

```python
# Each value held for 4 steps
d1 >> pluck(hpf=PStep([200, 800, 400, 1200], holds=[4, 4, 4, 4]), dur=1/16)

# Default: 1 step each
d1 >> pluck(degree=PStep([0, 4, 7, 12]))
```

### SC-side Modulation FX

#### `envmod` — ADSR Amplitude Modulator

Applies an ADSR envelope to the signal amplitude. Crossfades with dry signal via the `envmod` parameter.

```python
# Standard ADSR envelope
d1 >> pluck(envmod=1, ematk=0.01, emdec=0.2, emslev=0.6, emrel=0.3)

# Slow pad swell
d1 >> pads(envmod=1, ematk=0.5, emdec=0.3, emslev=0.8, emrel=0.5)

# Partial envelope blend
d1 >> pluck(envmod=0.5, ematk=0.1, emdec=0.4, emslev=0.3, emrel=0.1)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `envmod` | `0` | Dry/wet (0=bypass, 1=full envelope) |
| `ematk` | `0.01` | Attack time (fraction of sus) |
| `emdec` | `0.3` | Decay time (fraction of sus) |
| `emslev` | `0.7` | Sustain level (0-1) |
| `emrel` | `0.2` | Release time (fraction of sus) |
| `emcurve` | `-4` | Envelope curve (negative=fast decay) |

#### `envfilt` — ADSR Envelope Filter

ADSR-shaped filter sweep with selectable filter type.

```python
# Acid bass (fast attack, short decay)
d1 >> bass(envfilt=1, efstart=200, efpeak=6000, efattk=0.01, efdec=0.3, efsus=0.2, efres=0.3)

# Slow filter sweep
d1 >> pads(envfilt=1, efstart=500, efpeak=12000, efattk=0.3, efdec=0.5, efsus=0.6, efres=0.5)

# HPF envelope (eftype=1)
d1 >> pluck(envfilt=1, eftype=1, efstart=100, efpeak=4000, efdec=0.5)

# BPF envelope (eftype=2)
d1 >> pads(envfilt=0.8, eftype=2, efstart=300, efpeak=3000, efres=0.1)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `envfilt` | `0` | Dry/wet |
| `efstart` | `200` | Start frequency |
| `efpeak` | `8000` | Peak frequency |
| `efattk` | `0.01` | Attack time |
| `efdec` | `0.3` | Decay time |
| `efsus` | `0.5` | Sustain level (0-1, interpolates start↔peak) |
| `efrel` | `0.2` | Release time |
| `efcurve` | `-4` | Curve shape |
| `efres` | `0.5` | Filter resonance |
| `eftype` | `0` | 0=LPF, 1=HPF, 2=BPF |

#### `lfomod` — Multi-Shape LFO Amplitude Modulator

LFO-driven tremolo with 6 waveform shapes and optional beat sync.

```python
# Sine tremolo
d1 >> pluck(lfomod=-0.6, lmrate=1)

# Triangle, beat-synced
d1 >> pluck(lfomod=0.8, lmrate=4, lmshape=1, lmsync=1)

# Square gate
d1 >> pads(lfomod=1, lmrate=8, lmshape=3)

# Smooth random modulation
d1 >> pluck(lfomod=0.5, lmrate=2
            , lmshape=4)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `lfomod` | `0` | Dry/wet (depth) |
| `lmrate` | `4` | LFO rate (Hz, or beats if synced) |
| `lmshape` | `0` | 0=sin, 1=tri, 2=saw, 3=pulse, 4=smooth noise, 5=S&H |
| `lmphase` | `0` | LFO starting phase |
| `lmsync` | `0` | 0=free Hz, 1=beat-synced |

#### `lfofilt` — Multi-Shape LFO Filter

LFO-controlled filter with selectable waveform and filter type.

```python
# Auto-wah (sine LFO)
d1 >> bass(lfofilt=1, lfcenter=1500, lfdepth=1200, lfrate=2, lfres=0.3)

# Saw sweep filter
d1 >> pads(lfofilt=1, lfcenter=3000, lfdepth=2000, lfrate=1, lfshape=2)

# Beat-synced triangle filter
d1 >> pluck(lfofilt=1, lfcenter=2000, lfdepth=1500, lfrate=4, lfshape=1, lfsync=1)

# Random filter with HPF
d1 >> bass(lfofilt=0.7, lftype=1, lfcenter=1000, lfdepth=800, lfrate=3, lfshape=4)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `lfofilt` | `0` | Dry/wet |
| `lfcenter` | `2000` | Center frequency |
| `lfdepth` | `1500` | LFO depth in Hz |
| `lfrate` | `2` | LFO rate |
| `lfshape` | `0` | 0=sin, 1=tri, 2=saw, 3=pulse, 4=smooth noise, 5=S&H |
| `lfres` | `0.5` | Filter resonance |
| `lftype` | `0` | 0=LPF, 1=HPF, 2=BPF |
| `lfsync` | `0` | 0=free Hz, 1=beat-synced |

#### `vocoder` — Band Vocoder

8-band vocoder that imposes the spectral envelope of the input onto a carrier oscillator.

```python
# Classic vocoder with saw carrier
d1 >> pads(vocoder=0.7, vocfreq=100, vocq=0.03)

# Pulse carrier for buzzy tone
d1 >> pads(vocoder=0.8, voccarrier=1, vocfreq=80)

# Noise carrier for whisper effect
d1 >> pads(vocoder=0.6, voccarrier=2, vocq=0.05)
```

## 1. Generative Patterns

Algorithmic pattern generators that produce evolving, non-repeating sequences.

### PMarkov2 — Higher-order Markov chain

Analyzes an input sequence and builds N-gram transition tables. Falls back to shorter context windows when no exact match is found.

```python
# Train on a melody, generate new notes in the same style
d1 >> pluck(degree=[0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 5, 4, 2], dur=0.5)

# Order 1 = more random, order 3 = closer to source
d1 >> pluck(degree=PMarkov2([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1], order=9), dur=1/4)

# Use with scale degrees for generative melodies
d1 >> keys(degree=PMarkov2([0, 2, 4, 7, 9, 7, 4, 2, 0], order=3), sus=2, dur=1)
```

**Parameters:** `data` (source sequence), `order` (N-gram depth, default 2)

### PLife — Cellular automaton

1D elementary cellular automaton (Wolfram Rules 30, 90, 110, etc.) mapped to 0/1 values. Useful for binary rhythms and gates.

```python
# Rule 30 rhythm (chaotic)
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=30, size=16))

# Rule 110 (complex) as degree selection
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLife(rule=110, size=8) * 7, dur=0.5)

# Combine rules for layered rhythms
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=30, size=32))
d2 >> play("o", dur=0.25, amplify=PLife(rule=90, size=32))
```

**Parameters:** `rule` (rule number, default 30), `size` (grid width, default 16), `row` (starting row, default 0)

### PLSystem — L-system rewriting

L-system string rewriting mapped to numeric values. Default is Fibonacci L-system.

```python
# Default Fibonacci L-system
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLSystem(), dur=0.5)

# Custom L-system with custom mapping
d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PLSystem(
        axiom="A",
        rules={"A": "AB", "B": "A"},
        generations=8,
        mapping={"A": 0, "B": 4}
    ),
    dur=0.25
)

# Plant-like branching pattern
d1 >> keys(
    degree=PLSystem(axiom="F", rules={"F": "F+F-F"}, generations=4,
                    mapping={"F": 0, "+": 3, "-": -2}),
    dur=0.5, sus=2
)
```

**Parameters:** `axiom` (start string), `rules` (rewrite dict), `generations` (default 6), `mapping` (char-to-value dict)

### PEvolve — Genetic algorithm

Maintains a population of sequences, selects via tournament, crosses over, mutates, and walks through individuals.

```python
# Evolve a melody toward consonance
  
def consonance(seq):
    return sum(1 for x in seq if x in [0, 2, 4, 5, 7])

d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PEvolve([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], fitness=consonance, mutation=0.3),
    dur=0.5
)

# Evolve rhythmic density
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25,
    amplify=PEvolve([1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1],
                     fitness=lambda s: -abs(sum(s) - 5),  # target 5 hits
                     mutation=0.15))
```

**Parameters:** `population` (source values), `fitness` (fitness function), `mutation` (rate, default 0.1), `crossover` (rate, default 0.7), `pop_size` (default 8)

## 2. Stochastic Patterns

Probability-based and noise generators for humanization and controlled randomness.

### PGauss — Gaussian distribution

```python
# Humanized timing (slight random delay)
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.5, delay=PGauss(mean=0, sigma=0.02))

# Pitch variation around a center note
d1 >> pluck(degree=PGauss(4, 1), dur=0.5)

# Random velocity with normal distribution
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PGauss(mean=0.7, sigma=0.15))
```

**Parameters:** `mean` (center, default 0), `sigma` (std deviation, default 1)

### PBrown — Brownian motion

Constrained random walk. Each step adds a gaussian offset clamped to [lo, hi].

```python
# Drifting filter cutoff
d1 >> pluck(dur=0.5, lpf=PBrown(lo=200, hi=4000, step=100))

# Wandering pitch
d1 >> sine(degree=PBrown(lo=0, hi=7, step=1), dur=0.25)

# Slow panning drift
d1 >> pads(dur=2, pan=PBrown(lo=-1, hi=1, step=0.2))
```

**Parameters:** `lo` (lower bound, default 0), `hi` (upper bound, default 1), `step` (step size, default 0.1)

### PLogistic — Chaotic map

Logistic map: `x = r*x*(1-x)`. Produces chaos near r=3.9-4.0.

```python
# Chaotic pitch sequence
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLogistic(r=3.60, scale=1), dur=0.25)

# Edge of chaos (r=3.57 = period doubling)
d1 >> pluck(degree=PLogistic(r=3.57, scale=12, offset=-6), dur=0.5)

# Chaotic rhythm density
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PLogistic(r=3.5, scale=1))
```

**Parameters:** `r` (growth rate, default 3.9), `x0` (initial value, default 0.5), `scale` (output scale, default 1), `offset` (default 0)

### PSkip — Probability gate

Passes source values with a given probability, otherwise returns a default value.

```python
# Sparse hi-hat pattern (50% chance of playing)
d1 >> play("-", dur=0.25, amplify=PSkip(P[1], prob=0.5, default=0))

# Random note omission
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 5, 7], dur=0.5,
            amplify=PSkip(P[1], prob=0.7, default=0))

# Ghost notes on snare
d2 >> play("o", dur=0.5, amplify=PSkip(P[0.3], prob=0.4, default=0))
```

**Parameters:** `pattern` (source), `prob` (probability, default 0.5), `default` (fallback value, default 0)

### PSwitch — Weighted pattern switching

Each step randomly selects one of the source patterns based on weights.

```python
# Switch between two melodies
d1 >> pluck(
    degree=PSwitch([P[0, 2, 4], P[5, 7, 9]], weights=[0.7, 0.3]),
    dur=0.5
)

# Weighted rhythm switching
d1 >> play(
    PSwitch([P["x o x o"], P["x x . x"], P["x . x ."]], weights=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2]),
    dur=0.25
)
```

**Parameters:** `patterns` (list of patterns), `weights` (selection weights, default equal)

## 4. Advanced Euclidean Rhythms

Extensions to the built-in PEuclid for more complex rhythmic structures.

### PEuclidR — Rotated Euclidean

```python
# Standard Euclidean: 5 hits in 8 steps
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclid(5, 8))

d2 >> play("o", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidR(5, 8, rotation=2))


**Parameters:** `n` (pulses), `k` (steps), `rotation` (default 1)

### PEuclidFill — Layered Euclidean

OR-combines multiple Euclidean rhythms. Returns 1 where any layer has a pulse.

```python
# Layer 3-in-8 and 5-in-8
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidFill((3, 8), ([9, 3], 12)))

# Dense polyrhythmic fill
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amp=1,amplify=PEuclidFill((3, 16), (5, 8), (7, 16)))
```

**Parameters:** `*pairs` (tuples of (n, k) — all must share the same k)

### PEuclidAccent — Euclidean with accents

Two-layer Euclidean: base hits + accent layer. Returns 0 (rest), 0.5 (normal), or 1.0 (accent).

```python
# 5-in-8 with accented subset
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidAccent(5, 8, accent_n=2))

# 7-in-16 with 3 accents
d1 >> play("x", dur=0.25, amplify=PEuclidAccent(7, 16, accent_n=3))
```

**Parameters:** `n`, `k`, `accent_n` (default n//2), `accent_k` (default k)

## 5. Polymetric Tools

Duration pattern helpers for tuplets and metric divisions.

### PMetric — N pulses in M beats

```python
# 5 evenly-spaced notes in 4 beats
d1 >> pluck(dur=PMetric(5, 4))

# 7 notes in 2 beats
d2 >> bass(dur=PMetric(7, 2))

# 3 in 1 beat (= triplet)
d3 >> keys(dur=PMetric(3, 1))
```

**Parameters:** `pulses`, `period` (default 1)

### PTriplet — Triplet shorthand

```python
# Triplets against quarter notes
d1 >> pluck(dur=1)
d2 >> pluck(dur=PTriplet(1), oct=5)

# Half-note triplets
d3 >> bass(dur=PTriplet(2))
```

**Parameters:** `dur` (default 1)

### PQuintuplet — Quintuplet shorthand

```python

d1 >> pluck(dur=PQuintuplet(2))

# 5 in 1 beat
d2 >> pluck(dur=PQuintuplet(1), oct=5)
```

**Parameters:** `dur` (default 1)

### PPolymetric — Merged polymetric timeline

Merges multiple (pulses, value) pairs into a single interleaved timeline. Returns a dict with `dur` and `degree` patterns.

```python
# 3-against-4 polyrhythm
poly = PPolymetric((3, 0), (4, 2), total=4)
d1 >> pluck(dur=poly['dur'], degree=poly['degree'])

# 5-against-3 with different pitches

d1 >> pluck(dur=poly['dur'], degree=poly['degree'])
```

**Parameters:** `*divisions` (tuples of (pulses, value)), `total` (beats, default 4)

## 6. Spatial Audio Patterns

Pattern helpers and FX for stereo/multichannel spatial movement.

### POrbit — Sine pan positions

Pre-computed sine wave positions for the `pan` attribute.

```python
# Slow circular pan (16 steps)
d1 >> pluck(pan=POrbit(0.25, 1.0, 16), dur=0.25)

d1 >> pluck(amp=POrbit(0.25, 1.0, 16), dur=0.25)

  
# Fast narrow orbit
d1 >> pluck(amp=POrbit(1.0, 0.5, 8), dur=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `speed` (rotation speed, default 0.25), `width` (stereo width, default 1.0), `steps` (resolution, default 16)

### PStereo — Map values to stereo field

Normalizes any value list to the [-width, width] stereo range.

```python
# Map scale degrees to stereo positions
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7], amp=PStereo([0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7]))

# Narrow stereo field
d1 >> pluck(pan=PStereo([0, 3, 7, 5], width=0.5))
```

**Parameters:** `values` (input list), `width` (stereo width, default 1.0)

### orbit — Orbital Pan FX

Server-side circular stereo panning synced to tempo.

```python
# Slow orbit
d1 >> pluck(orbit=0.25, orbitwidth=1)

# Fast narrow circle
d1 >> pads(orbit=2, orbitwidth=0.5)

# Varying orbit speed
d1 >> pluck(orbit=linvar([0.1, 2], 16), orbitwidth=0.8, dur=1/4)
```

**Parameters:** `orbit` (speed, synced to beat_dur), `orbitwidth` (0-1, default 1)

### fspread — Frequency-dependent stereo spread

Splits audio into low/mid/high bands and pans each differently. Low stays center, highs go wide.

```python
# Wide frequency spread
d1 >> dbass(fspread=0.9, fspreadfreq=100)

# Subtle spread with low crossover
d1 >> pads(fspread=0.4, fspreadfreq=500)
```

**Parameters:** `fspread` (amount 0-1), `fspreadfreq` (crossover frequency, default 1000)

### rotate — Multichannel rotation

PanAz-based rotation for quad output systems.

```python
# Slow quad rotation
d1 >> dbass(rotate=0.25, rotwidth=1.5)

# Fast rotation
d1 >> pluck(rotate=2, rotwidth=2)
```

**Parameters:** `rotate` (speed, synced to beat_dur), `rotwidth` (focus width, default 1.5)

d2 >> bass(degree=follow(d1, 'degree', lambda x: x + 4))

## 10. Audio-Reactive System

Real-time audio analysis from SuperCollider fed back into Python patterns.

### Setup

```python
# Start analysis on a player
reactive(d1)
d1 >> dbass()
# Stop analysis
unreactive(d1)
```

### PAmp — Amplitude follower

Pattern that tracks another player's amplitude in real-time.

```python
# d2's filter follows d1's volume
d1 >> play("x o x o", dur=0.5)
reactive(d1)
d2 >> pads(lpf=PAmp(d1, scale=5000, smooth=0.3))

```

### POnset — Onset detection

Returns 1 on detected onsets, 0 otherwise.

reactive(d1)
d2 >> pluck(amplify=POnset(d1, threshold=1.9))
```

### PReact — Custom reactive mapping

Generic audio-reactive pattern with a custom function.

```python

```

## 11. Granular & Sample Manipulation SynthDefs

Buffer-based synths for granular processing, time-stretching, and slicing.

### grainX — Advanced granular synth

GrainBuf-based granular synthesis with fine-grained control.

```python
# Basic granular playback
d1 >> grainX("break16", pos=0.5, density=20, size=0.1, dur=4)

# Scanning through a sample
d1 >> grainX("break", pos=linvar([0, 1], 8), density=15, size=0.05)

# With slice positions
d1 >> grainX("break16", pos=slice_buf(16), dur=0.25, density=10, size=0.1)

# Spray and jitter for texture
d1 >> grainX("ambient", pos=0.3, density=30, size=0.2, spray=0.1, jitter=0.05)
```

**Parameters:** `pos` (0-1 buffer position), `density` (grains/sec, default 10), `size` (grain duration, default 0.1), `spray` (position randomness), `jitter` (timing randomness), `scan` (auto-scan), `shape` (envelope shape), `spread` (stereo spread)

### gsynth — TGrains granular synth

TGrains-based granular synthesis.

```python
# Granular texture
d1 >> gsynth("break", pos=0.5, density=10, size=0.5, dur=4)

# Pitch-shifted grains
d1 >> gsynth("break", pos=linvar([0, 1], 16), deg=0.5, density=20)

# Slice-based granular
d1 >> gsynth("break16", pos=slice_buf(8), dur=0.5, size=0.3)
```

**Parameters:** `pos` (buffer position), `density` (trigger rate, default 10), `size` (grain dur, default 0.5), `deg` (pitch ratio, default 1)

### timestretch — Warp1 time stretcher

Independent time and pitch control using Warp1.

```python
# Half-speed (double length)
d1 >> timestretch("break", stretchratio=2, sus=8)

# Double-speed
d1 >> timestretch("break", stretchratio=0.5, sus=2)

# Normal speed, smooth granular quality
d1 >> timestretch("break16
                  
                  ", stretchratio=1, windowSize=0.3, overlaps=12)

# Extreme stretch for ambient texture
d1 >> timestretch("ambient", stretchratio=8, sus=32, windowSize=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `stretchratio` (1=normal, 2=half-speed, 0.5=double-speed), `windowSize` (default 0.2), `overlaps` (quality, default 8)

### slicer — Buffer slice playback

Plays a normalized region of a buffer, automatically adjusting rate to fit the slice into `sus`.

```python
# Play first quarter of a sample
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=0, slice_end=0.25, sus=1)

# Play second half
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=0.5, slice_end=1.0, sus=2)

# Sequenced slices
d1 >> slicer("break", slice_start=P[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75],
                       slice_end=P[0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0], dur=0.5)

# Random slice selection
d1 >> slicer("break",
    slice_start=PRand(0, 0.75),
    slice_end=PRand(0.25, 1.0),
    dur=0.5)
```

**Parameters:** `slice_start` (0-1, default 0), `slice_end` (0-1, default 1)

### tstretch — Time stretch FX

PitchShift-based time manipulation applied as an effect on any synth. Preserves pitch.

```python
# Subtle time smear on a synth
d1 >> pluck(dur=0.5, tstretch=0.8, tstretchsize=1.0)

# Heavy granular processing
d1 >> bass(dur=1, tstretch=0.2, tstretchsize=0.1)

# Varying stretch amount
d1 >> pads(dur=2, tstretch=linvar([0.5, 2], 8))
```

**Parameters:** `tstretch` (ratio, 1=bypass), `tstretchsize` (grain window, default 0.2)

## 12. Live Looping

Real-time recording and looping system with overdub support.

### Basic usage

```python
# Create a 4-beat loop buffer
ll = LiveLooper(duration=4)
                  
                  

# Record from hardware input
ll.rec()                      # starts at next bar
ll.stop_rec()                 # stop recording

# Play back
d1 >> ll.play(beat_stretch=1, room=0.3)

# Overdub at 50% blend
ll.overdub(amount=0.5)
ll.stop_rec()
```

### Capture from another player

```python
# Record d1's output
d1 >> pluck(degree=P[0, 2, 4, 7], dur=0.5)
ll = LiveLooper(duration=8)
ll.from_player(d1)            # capture d1's audio
ll.stop_rec()
d2 >> ll.play(beat_stretch=1)
```

### Multiple loopers

```python
# Layer multiple loops
ll1 = LiveLooper(duration=4)
ll2 = LiveLooper(duration=8)

ll1.rec(channel=0)           # record from input channel 0
ll2.rec(channel=1)           # record from input channel 1

# Play both
d1 >> ll1.play(beat_stretch=1)
d2 >> ll2.play(beat_stretch=1, room=0.5)
```

### Cleanup

```python
ll.free()                     # stop recording and free buffer
```

## 14. Audio Effects Reference

All effects are applied as keyword arguments on any player. Organized by category.

### Envelope
d1 >> pluck(a=0.5, ac=3, rc=-1, position=0.3)
                  
| Parameter | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `leg=N` | Legato slide (XLine scaling) | `d1 >> pluck(leg=0.5)` |
| `a=T, ac=C` | Attack time with curve | `d1 >> pluck(a=0.5, ac=-3)` |
| `r=T, rc=C` | Release time with curve | `d1 >> pluck(r=0.5, rc=-3)` |
| `position=P` | Trim: silence before position (0-1 of sus) | `d1 >> pluck(position=0.5)` |
| `transient=T, transattack=A, transsustain=S` | Transient shaper | `d1 >> play("x", transient=0.8, transattack=2)` |
